teks.rationale: Students listen actively and ask relevant questions during a group discussion.

studentGoal.en: Plan a paragraph for the claim "Trees are important to our community" by sorting sentences: supporting details, sentences that only repeat the claim, and sentences that are off topic.
studentGoal.es: Planea un párrafo para la afirmación "Trees are important to our community" clasificando oraciones: detalles de apoyo, oraciones que solo repiten la afirmación y oraciones que no tienen que ver con el tema.

studentDirections.en: The claim is: "Trees are important to our community." Sort each sentence. Does it give a supporting detail, only repeat the claim, or go off topic? Then write your paragraph with the supporting details.
studentDirections.es: La afirmación es: "Trees are important to our community" (Los árboles son importantes para nuestra comunidad). Clasifica cada oración. ¿Da un detalle de apoyo, solo repite la afirmación o se sale del tema? Luego escribe tu párrafo con los detalles de apoyo.

teacherDirections.en: Write the claim on the board. The key teaching move is the middle bin: a sentence that just says "trees are important" again sounds on-topic but adds no support. The trickiest item is "Some trees lose their leaves in fall," which is true and about trees but does not show why trees matter. After sorting, students write a paragraph: the claim, three supporting details joined with "also" or "in addition," and a closing sentence.
teacherDirections.es: Escribe la afirmación en el pizarrón. La clave es la categoría del medio: una oración que solo vuelve a decir que "los árboles son importantes" parece del tema pero no agrega apoyo. El ítem más difícil es "Some trees lose their leaves in fall": es cierto y habla de árboles, pero no muestra por qué los árboles importan. Después de clasificar, los estudiantes escriben un párrafo: la afirmación, tres detalles de apoyo unidos con "also" o "in addition" y una oración de cierre.

languageFunction.en: Selecting supporting details to justify a claim in writing.
languageFunction.es: Seleccionar detalles de apoyo para justificar una afirmación por escrito.

label.en: Supporting detail
label.es: Detalle de apoyo

hint.en: Gives a fact or example that shows WHY trees are important.
hint.es: Da un dato o ejemplo que muestra POR QUÉ los árboles son importantes.

label.en: Only repeats the claim
label.es: Solo repite la afirmación

hint.en: Says trees are important again, but gives no new reason.
hint.es: Vuelve a decir que los árboles son importantes, pero no da una razón nueva.

label.en: Off topic
label.es: Fuera del tema

hint.en: Does not help prove that trees are important to the community.
hint.es: No ayuda a demostrar que los árboles son importantes para la comunidad.

prompt.en: Trees give shade that keeps sidewalks and houses cooler in summer.
prompt.es: Trees give shade that keeps sidewalks and houses cooler in summer.

high.en: In Spanish: Los árboles dan sombra que mantiene más frescas las banquetas y las casas en verano.
high.es: En español: Los árboles dan sombra que mantiene más frescas las banquetas y las casas en verano.

why.en: This is a fact that shows one way trees help the community: they keep things cooler.
why.es: Es un dato que muestra una manera en que los árboles ayudan a la comunidad: mantienen las cosas más frescas.

hint.en: Does it give a reason trees matter?
hint.es: ¿Da una razón por la que los árboles importan?

prompt.en: Trees are really, really important.

high.en: In Spanish: Los árboles son muy, muy importantes.
high.es: En español: Los árboles son muy, muy importantes.

why.en: This just says the claim again with "really, really." It gives no fact or example, so it does not support anything.
why.es: Esto solo vuelve a decir la afirmación con "really, really." No da ningún dato ni ejemplo, así que no apoya nada.

hint.en: Does it tell WHY?
hint.es: ¿Dice POR QUÉ?

prompt.en: My cousin has a red bike.
prompt.es: My cousin has a red bike.

high.en: In Spanish: Mi primo tiene una bicicleta roja.
high.es: En español: Mi primo tiene una bicicleta roja.

why.en: This is not about trees at all, so it does not belong in this paragraph.
why.es: Esto no habla de árboles para nada, así que no va en este párrafo.

hint.en: Is this about trees?
hint.es: ¿Esto habla de árboles?

prompt.en: Tree roots hold the soil in place so rain does not wash it away.
prompt.es: Tree roots hold the soil in place so rain does not wash it away.

high.en: In Spanish: Las raíces de los árboles sostienen la tierra para que la lluvia no se la lleve.
high.es: En español: Las raíces de los árboles sostienen la tierra para que la lluvia no se la lleve.

why.en: This explains a real benefit: roots stop soil from washing away. That supports the claim.
why.es: Esto explica un beneficio real: las raíces evitan que la tierra se deslave. Eso apoya la afirmación.

hint.en: What do roots do for the land?
hint.es: ¿Qué hacen las raíces por la tierra?

prompt.en: Some trees lose their leaves in fall.
prompt.es: Some trees lose their leaves in fall.

high.en: In Spanish: Algunos árboles pierden sus hojas en otoño.
high.es: En español: Algunos árboles pierden sus hojas en otoño.

why.en: This is true and it is about trees, but it does not show why trees are important to the community. Supporting details must prove the claim, not just share the topic.
why.es: Es cierto y habla de árboles, pero no muestra por qué los árboles son importantes para la comunidad. Los detalles de apoyo deben demostrar la afirmación, no solo tratar el mismo tema.

hint.en: It is about trees, but does it show they are IMPORTANT?
hint.es: Habla de árboles, pero ¿muestra que son IMPORTANTES?

prompt.en: Our community needs trees because trees are important.
prompt.es: Our community needs trees because trees are important.

high.en: In Spanish: Nuestra comunidad necesita árboles porque los árboles son importantes.
high.es: En español: Nuestra comunidad necesita árboles porque los árboles son importantes.

why.en: This sentence has "because," but the reason is the claim itself. A real reason gives new information.
why.es: Esta oración tiene "because", pero la razón es la misma afirmación. Una razón real da información nueva.

hint.en: Is the "because" part new information?
hint.es: ¿La parte con "because" es información nueva?

prompt.en: Birds and squirrels build their nests in trees.
prompt.es: Birds and squirrels build their nests in trees.

high.en: In Spanish: Los pájaros y las ardillas hacen sus nidos en los árboles.
high.es: En español: Los pájaros y las ardillas hacen sus nidos en los árboles.

why.en: This is an example of trees giving homes to animals in the community, so it supports the claim.
why.es: Es un ejemplo de cómo los árboles dan hogar a los animales de la comunidad, así que apoya la afirmación.

hint.en: Who else lives in our community?
hint.es: ¿Quién más vive en nuestra comunidad?

prompt.en: The library opens at 9:00 on Saturdays.
prompt.es: The library opens at 9:00 on Saturdays.

high.en: In Spanish: La biblioteca abre a las 9:00 los sábados.
high.es: En español: La biblioteca abre a las 9:00 los sábados.

why.en: This is about the community, but not about trees, so it does not help prove the claim.
why.es: Esto habla de la comunidad, pero no de los árboles, así que no ayuda a demostrar la afirmación.

hint.en: Does it mention trees?
hint.es: ¿Menciona los árboles?

prompt.en: Leaves take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen.
prompt.es: Leaves take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen.

high.en: In Spanish: Las hojas absorben dióxido de carbono y liberan oxígeno.
high.es: En español: Las hojas absorben dióxido de carbono y liberan oxígeno.

why.en: This science fact shows trees help the air we breathe, which is a strong supporting detail.
why.es: Este dato de ciencias muestra que los árboles ayudan al aire que respiramos: es un detalle de apoyo fuerte.

hint.en: How does this help people?
hint.es: ¿Cómo ayuda esto a las personas?

elps.rationale: Students derive meaning from short content sentences, with home-language support, to judge whether each supports a claim.
Selecting supporting details is the planning step for writing to justify a claim with supporting details and evidence, which students then do.
Grade 3 students derive meaning from short content sentences, with visual and linguistic supports, to judge whether each supports a claim.

teks.rationale: Students distinguish evidence that supports a response from sentences that only restate it or are off topic.

title.es: Del mensaje de texto al correo electrónico

studentGoal.en: Turn a quick text-message idea into a clear, respectful email to a teacher — with a subject line, greeting, polite request, and closing.
studentGoal.es: Convierte una idea rápida de mensaje de texto en un correo electrónico claro y respetuoso para un maestro, con asunto, saludo, petición cortés y despedida.

studentDirections.en: Each item shows how you might text a friend. Choose the version that belongs in an email to your teacher. Choose, then select Check.
studentDirections.es: Cada ejercicio muestra cómo le escribirías un mensaje a un amigo. Elige la versión que corresponde a un correo electrónico para tu maestra. Elige y luego selecciona Revisar.

teacherDirections.en: Students often write to teachers the way they text friends. Walk through one email part per item: subject line, greeting, explanation, request, closing. Distractors are either texting style (abbreviations, “lol,” no capitals) or demanding in tone. After the activity, have students assemble the five correct parts into one complete email and read it aloud.
teacherDirections.es: Los estudiantes a menudo les escriben a los maestros como si enviaran mensajes a sus amigos. Repasen una parte del correo en cada ejercicio: asunto, saludo, explicación, petición y despedida. Los distractores usan estilo de mensaje de texto (abreviaturas, “lol”, sin mayúsculas) o un tono exigente. Después de la actividad, pide a los estudiantes que unan las cinco partes correctas en un correo completo y lo lean en voz alta.

languageFunction.en: Adjusting register, tone, and conventions from informal texting to a formal written request.
languageFunction.es: Ajustar el registro, el tono y las convenciones del mensaje de texto informal a una petición escrita formal.

context.en: You missed class on Monday. To a friend you would text: “hey can i get the hw i missed.” Now you are emailing your teacher, Ms. Garza.
context.es: Faltaste a clase el lunes. A un amigo le escribirías: “hey can i get the hw i missed.” Ahora le escribes un correo a tu maestra, Ms. Garza.

prompt.en: Which opening fits an email to a teacher?
prompt.es: ¿Qué inicio es adecuado para un correo a una maestra?

high.en: Frame: “Dear Ms. ___, I was absent on ___ and missed ___.” / Marco: “Dear” = “Estimada”.
high.es: Marco: “Dear Ms. ___, I was absent on ___ and missed ___.” (“Dear” = “Estimada”).

medium.en: Start with a greeting and the teacher's name, then explain.
medium.es: Empieza con un saludo y el nombre de la maestra; luego explica.

label.en: “hey ms g!! i was out on monday, can i get the hw u gave us”
label.es: “hey ms g!! i was out on monday, can i get the hw u gave us”

label.en: “Dear Ms. Garza, I was absent on Monday and missed the homework.”
label.es: “Dear Ms. Garza, I was absent on Monday and missed the homework.”

label.en: “Ms. Garza — I missed Monday. Send me the homework now, please.”
label.es: “Ms. Garza — I missed Monday. Send me the homework now, please.”

why.en: “hey,” a nickname, double exclamation points, “hw,” and “u” are texting style for friends. An email to a teacher opens with a greeting such as “Dear Ms. Garza.”
why.es: “hey”, un apodo, dos signos de exclamación, “hw” y “u” son estilo de mensaje para amigos. Un correo a una maestra empieza con un saludo como “Dear Ms. Garza.”

hint.en: Look for “Dear” plus the teacher's name.
hint.es: Busca “Dear” más el nombre de la maestra.

why.en: Right. A formal greeting with the teacher's name, followed by one clear sentence about what happened, sets a respectful register.
why.es: Correcto. Un saludo formal con el nombre de la maestra, seguido de una oración clara sobre lo que pasó, establece un registro respetuoso.

why.en: This sounds like an order. “Send me… now” makes the message demanding, even with “please” at the end. Open with a greeting and explain calmly.
why.es: Esto suena como una orden. “Send me… now” hace que el mensaje sea exigente, aunque termine con “please”. Empieza con un saludo y explica con calma.

hint.en: Explain your situation before you ask.
hint.es: Explica tu situación antes de pedir algo.

context.en: Your email needs a subject line so Ms. Garza knows what it is about before she opens it.
context.es: Tu correo necesita un asunto para que Ms. Garza sepa de qué trata antes de abrirlo.

prompt.en: Which subject line is clear and appropriate?

high.en: A subject line names the topic in a few words: what + when. / El asunto nombra el tema en pocas palabras: qué + cuándo.
high.es: El asunto nombra el tema en pocas palabras: qué + cuándo.

medium.en: Which one tells the teacher exactly what the email is about?
medium.es: ¿Cuál le dice a la maestra exactamente de qué trata el correo?

label.en: “Missing homework from Monday, 3rd period”
label.es: “Missing homework from Monday, 3rd period”

label.en: “u there? need to ask u something about class”
label.es: “u there? need to ask u something about class”

why.en: Right. It names the topic (missing homework), the day, and the class period, so the teacher knows what you need before opening it.
why.es: Correcto. Nombra el tema (tarea que falta), el día y el periodo de clase, así la maestra sabe qué necesitas antes de abrirlo.

why.en: Punctuation alone gives no information and can seem alarming. A subject line should name the topic.
why.es: Los signos solos no dan información y pueden parecer alarmantes. El asunto debe nombrar el tema.

hint.en: Name the topic and the day.
hint.es: Nombra el tema y el día.

why.en: “u there?” is a text to a friend, and “something about class” does not say what the email is about. “u” is not used in school email.
why.es: “u there?” es un mensaje para un amigo, y “something about class” no dice de qué trata el correo. “u” no se usa en el correo escolar.

hint.en: Which choice names the topic?
hint.es: ¿Qué opción nombra el tema?

context.en: To a friend you would write: “can u send it.” Now write the request to Ms. Garza.
context.es: A un amigo le escribirías: “can u send it.” Ahora escribe la petición para Ms. Garza.

prompt.en: Which request is polite and specific?

high.en: Frame: “Could you please ___?” / “¿Podría por favor ___?”
high.es: Marco: “Could you please ___?” (= “¿Podría por favor ___?”).

medium.en: Polite requests often start with “Could you please…”
medium.es: Las peticiones corteses suelen empezar con “Could you please…”

label.en: “Send me the assignment from Monday right away.”
label.es: “Send me the assignment from Monday right away.”

label.en: “can u send me the stuff we did in class on monday lol, i was out”
label.es: “can u send me the stuff we did in class on monday lol, i was out”

label.en: “Could you please tell me where I can find Monday's assignment?”
label.es: “Could you please tell me where I can find Monday's assignment?”

why.en: This names the assignment, but it is a command with no “please,” and “right away” sounds demanding.
why.es: Esto nombra la tarea, pero es una orden sin “please”, y “right away” suena exigente.

hint.en: Add “Could you please…” to turn the command into a polite request.
hint.es: Agrega “Could you please…” para convertir la orden en una petición cortés.

why.en: “u” and “lol” belong in texts to friends, and “the stuff we did” is vague about what you need.
why.es: “u” y “lol” son para mensajes a amigos, y “the stuff we did” es vago sobre lo que necesitas.

hint.en: Use full words and say exactly what you need.
hint.es: Usa palabras completas y di exactamente qué necesitas.

why.en: Right. “Could you please” is polite, and “Monday's assignment” says exactly what you need.
why.es: Correcto. “Could you please” es cortés, y “Monday's assignment” dice exactamente lo que necesitas.

context.en: To a friend you would write: “i was sick so idk what we did.” Now explain this to Ms. Garza.
context.es: A un amigo le escribirías: “i was sick so idk what we did.” Ahora explícaselo a Ms. Garza.

prompt.en: Which sentence explains the situation in the right tone?
prompt.es: ¿Qué oración explica la situación con el tono adecuado?

high.en: Frame: “I was ___ on ___, so I am not sure ___.” Replace “idk” with “I am not sure.”
high.es: Marco: “I was ___ on ___, so I am not sure ___.” Cambia “idk” por “I am not sure” (= “no estoy seguro”).

medium.en: Write out the full words, and keep the tone calm and respectful.
medium.es: Escribe las palabras completas y mantén un tono tranquilo y respetuoso.

label.en: “I was sick and idk what happened lol”
label.es: “I was sick and idk what happened lol”

label.en: “I was sick on Monday, so I am not sure what we covered in class.”
label.es: “I was sick on Monday, so I am not sure what we covered in class.”

label.en: “Being sick is not my fault, so you need to tell me what I missed.”
label.es: “Being sick is not my fault, so you need to tell me what I missed.”

why.en: “idk” and “lol” are texting abbreviations. In an email to a teacher, write the full words: “I am not sure.”
why.es: “idk” y “lol” son abreviaturas de mensajes. En un correo a una maestra, escribe las palabras completas: “I am not sure.”

hint.en: Replace the abbreviations with full words.
hint.es: Cambia las abreviaturas por palabras completas.

why.en: Right. It gives the reason and the day, uses complete words, and sounds calm — exactly the tone a teacher expects.
why.es: Correcto. Da la razón y el día, usa palabras completas y suena tranquilo: justo el tono que espera una maestra.

why.en: The words are formal, but the tone is defensive and demanding (“you need to tell me”). Register includes tone, not just spelling.
why.es: Las palabras son formales, pero el tono es defensivo y exigente (“you need to tell me”). El registro incluye el tono, no solo la ortografía.

hint.en: Which choice sounds calm and respectful?
hint.es: ¿Qué opción suena tranquila y respetuosa?

context.en: To a friend you would end with: “thx bye.” Now close your email to Ms. Garza.
context.es: A un amigo le terminarías con: “thx bye.” Ahora cierra tu correo a Ms. Garza.

prompt.en: Which closing fits an email to a teacher?
prompt.es: ¿Qué despedida es adecuada para un correo a una maestra?

high.en: Frame: “Thank you for ___. Sincerely, [your full name]” / “Sincerely” = “Atentamente”.
high.es: Marco: “Thank you for ___. Sincerely, [tu nombre completo]” (“Sincerely” = “Atentamente”).

medium.en: Thank the teacher and sign with your full name.
medium.es: Dale las gracias a la maestra y firma con tu nombre completo.

label.en: “Thank you for your help. Sincerely, Daniel Ortiz”
label.es: “Thank you for your help. Sincerely, Daniel Ortiz”

label.en: “thx so much ms g, ttyl — daniel”
label.es: “thx so much ms g, ttyl — daniel”

label.en: “That's all I needed. Reply ASAP. — Daniel”
label.es: “That's all I needed. Reply ASAP. — Daniel”

why.en: Right. A thank-you, a formal closing (“Sincerely”), and your full name tell the teacher who wrote and end politely.
why.es: Correcto. Un agradecimiento, una despedida formal (“Sincerely”) y tu nombre completo le dicen a la maestra quién escribió y cierran con cortesía.

why.en: “thx” and “ttyl” are text abbreviations, and a nickname with a lowercase first name is not a formal closing.
why.es: “thx” y “ttyl” son abreviaturas de mensaje, y un apodo con solo tu nombre en minúscula no es una despedida formal.

hint.en: Write “Thank you” and sign your name.
hint.es: Escribe “Thank you” y firma con tu nombre.

why.en: “Reply ASAP” pressures the teacher, and there is no thank-you or formal closing. The closing should be polite.
why.es: “Reply ASAP” presiona a la maestra, y no hay agradecimiento ni despedida formal. La despedida debe ser cortés.

hint.en: End with thanks, not a demand.
hint.es: Termina con un agradecimiento, no con una exigencia.

elps.rationale: Students write a request using the register, style, and conventions suited to a teacher audience.
Contrasting texting and email language builds the formal register students also use when speaking to teachers in class.

studentGoal.en: Justify an answer or evaluate a classmate's claim with a clear reason and evidence, using academic sentence frames.
studentGoal.es: Justifica una respuesta o evalúa la afirmación de un compañero con una razón clara y evidencia, usando marcos de oración académicos.

studentDirections.en: Your teacher asks you to justify an answer or evaluate a claim. Choose the response that gives a correct claim AND a reason or evidence. Choose, then select Check.
studentDirections.es: Tu maestro te pide justificar una respuesta o evaluar una afirmación. Elige la respuesta que da una afirmación correcta Y una razón o evidencia. Elige y luego selecciona Revisar.

teacherDirections.en: “Justify” and “evaluate” are task words students meet in every content area. Each item has one response with a claim plus specific evidence, and distractors that give no reason, a circular reason, or a flawed reason. Use the CLEAR overlay: name the claim, then point to the evidence. Post the frames and have partners say each correct response aloud before writing their own for a new problem.
teacherDirections.es: “Justificar” y “evaluar” son palabras de instrucción que los estudiantes encuentran en todas las materias. Cada ejercicio tiene una respuesta con afirmación y evidencia específica, y distractores sin razón, con razón circular o con razonamiento erróneo. Usa el apoyo CLEAR: nombra la afirmación y luego señala la evidencia. Publica los marcos y pide a las parejas que digan cada respuesta correcta en voz alta antes de escribir la suya para un problema nuevo.

languageFunction.en: Justifying and evaluating claims orally with reasons and evidence.
languageFunction.es: Justificar y evaluar afirmaciones oralmente con razones y evidencia.

context.en: Math: Your teacher asks, “Is 3/4 greater than 2/3? Justify your answer.”
context.es: Matemáticas: Tu maestro pregunta: “Is 3/4 greater than 2/3? Justify your answer.”

prompt.en: Which response justifies the answer best?

high.en: Frames: “I know ___ because ___.” / “The evidence that supports this is ___.” / “I agree / disagree with ___ because ___.”
high.es: Marcos: “I know ___ because ___.” (= “Sé que ___ porque ___”) / “The evidence that supports this is ___.” / “I agree / disagree with ___ because ___.”

medium.en: A justification shows HOW you know — for example, with common denominators.
medium.es: Una justificación muestra CÓMO lo sabes; por ejemplo, con denominadores comunes.

label.en: “Yes, 3/4 is bigger. I just know it, and it looks bigger in my head.”
label.es: “Yes, 3/4 is bigger. I just know it, and it looks bigger in my head.”

label.en: “Yes. 3/4 = 9/12 and 2/3 = 8/12, and 9/12 is greater than 8/12, so 3/4 is greater.”
label.es: “Yes. 3/4 = 9/12 and 2/3 = 8/12, and 9/12 is greater than 8/12, so 3/4 is greater.”

label.en: “Yes, because 4 is bigger than 3, so 3/4 must be the bigger fraction.”
label.es: “Yes, because 4 is bigger than 3, so 3/4 must be the bigger fraction.”

why.en: The claim is correct, but “I just know it” and “it looks bigger” give no reason. Justifying means showing how you know.
why.es: La afirmación es correcta, pero “I just know it” y “it looks bigger” no dan ninguna razón. Justificar significa mostrar cómo lo sabes.

hint.en: Which choice shows the math?
hint.es: ¿Qué opción muestra las matemáticas?

why.en: Right. Rewriting both fractions with the denominator 12 is evidence anyone can check, and the conclusion follows from it.
why.es: Correcto. Escribir ambas fracciones con denominador 12 es evidencia que cualquiera puede comprobar, y la conclusión se deriva de ella.

why.en: The answer is right, but the reason is wrong: a bigger denominator means SMALLER pieces, so comparing 4 and 3 does not prove anything here.
why.es: La respuesta es correcta, pero la razón no: un denominador mayor significa partes MÁS PEQUEÑAS, así que comparar 4 y 3 no prueba nada aquí.

hint.en: Try a reason that compares equal-sized pieces.
hint.es: Busca una razón que compare partes del mismo tamaño.

context.en: Science: “Is an ice cube melting a physical change or a chemical change? Justify.”
context.es: Ciencias: “Is an ice cube melting a physical change or a chemical change? Justify.”

prompt.en: Which response justifies the answer best?

high.en: Frames: “I know ___ because ___.” / “The evidence that supports this is ___.” / “I agree / disagree with ___ because ___.”
high.es: Marcos: “I know ___ because ___.” (= “Sé que ___ porque ___”) / “The evidence that supports this is ___.” / “I agree / disagree with ___ because ___.”

medium.en: Ask: does a NEW substance form?
medium.es: Pregúntate: ¿se forma una sustancia NUEVA?

label.en: “It is a physical change because the ice goes from solid to liquid but is still water; no new substance forms.”
label.es: “It is a physical change because the ice goes from solid to liquid but is still water; no new substance forms.”

label.en: “It is a physical change because my partner said so, and she always gets science questions right.”
label.es: “It is a physical change because my partner said so, and she always gets science questions right.”

label.en: “It is a chemical change because it looks different, and the solid ice turns into a puddle of liquid.”
label.es: “It is a chemical change because it looks different, and the solid ice turns into a puddle of liquid.”

why.en: Right. The claim (physical change) is supported by the key evidence: the substance is still water, so nothing new formed.
why.es: Correcto. La afirmación (cambio físico) se apoya en la evidencia clave: la sustancia sigue siendo agua, así que no se formó nada nuevo.

why.en: A classmate's opinion — even a classmate who is usually right — is not scientific evidence. Explain what happens to the substance itself.
why.es: La opinión de una compañera, aunque casi siempre acierte, no es evidencia científica. Explica qué le pasa a la sustancia misma.

hint.en: Use evidence about the water, not about a person.
hint.es: Usa evidencia sobre el agua, no sobre una persona.

why.en: Looking different is not enough — solid to liquid is a change of state, and the puddle is still water. A chemical change makes a new substance.
why.es: Verse diferente no es suficiente: pasar de sólido a líquido es un cambio de estado, y el charco sigue siendo agua. Un cambio químico forma una sustancia nueva.

hint.en: Did a new substance form?
hint.es: ¿Se formó una sustancia nueva?

context.en: Science: A classmate claims, “Heavier objects always fall faster, so on the Moon a hammer will land before a feather.”
context.es: Ciencias: Un compañero afirma: “Heavier objects always fall faster, so on the Moon a hammer will land before a feather.”

prompt.en: Which response evaluates the claim with a reason?
prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta evalúa la afirmación con una razón?

high.en: Frames: “I know ___ because ___.” / “The evidence that supports this is ___.” / “I agree / disagree with ___ because ___.”
high.es: Marcos: “I know ___ because ___.” (= “Sé que ___ porque ___”) / “The evidence that supports this is ___.” / “I agree / disagree with ___ because ___.”

medium.en: The Moon has no air. Without air resistance, objects fall at the same rate.
medium.es: La Luna no tiene aire. Sin resistencia del aire, los objetos caen a la misma velocidad.

label.en: “That's a bad idea, and honestly anyone who has ever dropped a hammer and a feather knows it.”
label.es: “That's a bad idea, and honestly anyone who has ever dropped a hammer and a feather knows it.”

label.en: “I'm not sure, maybe. A hammer is a lot heavier than a feather, so it could land first, but who knows?”
label.es: “I'm not sure, maybe. A hammer is a lot heavier than a feather, so it could land first, but who knows?”

label.en: “I disagree, because the Moon has no air resistance, so both fall at the same rate. Apollo 15 astronauts tested it.”
label.es: “I disagree, because the Moon has no air resistance, so both fall at the same rate. Apollo 15 astronauts tested it.”

why.en: This judges the idea but gives no scientific reason. Evaluating means explaining WHY a claim is or isn't supported.
why.es: Esto juzga la idea pero no da ninguna razón científica. Evaluar significa explicar POR QUÉ una afirmación tiene o no tiene apoyo.

hint.en: Use “I disagree because ___.”
hint.es: Usa “I disagree because ___.”

why.en: This avoids taking a position and repeats the classmate's mistake. To evaluate, state whether you agree and give a scientific reason.
why.es: Esto evita tomar una postura y repite el error del compañero. Para evaluar, di si estás de acuerdo y da una razón científica.

hint.en: Take a position and support it.
hint.es: Toma una postura y apóyala.

why.en: Right. It states a position, gives the scientific reason (no air resistance), and adds evidence from a real test on the Moon.
why.es: Correcto. Expresa una postura, da la razón científica (no hay resistencia del aire) y agrega evidencia de una prueba real en la Luna.

context.en: Social studies: “Why did many early Texas towns grow up along rivers? Justify your answer.”
context.es: Estudios sociales: “Why did many early Texas towns grow up along rivers? Justify your answer.”

prompt.en: Which response justifies the answer best?

high.en: Frames: “I know ___ because ___.” / “The evidence that supports this is ___.” / “I agree / disagree with ___ because ___.”
high.es: Marcos: “I know ___ because ___.” (= “Sé que ___ porque ___”) / “The evidence that supports this is ___.” / “I agree / disagree with ___ because ___.”

medium.en: Think: what did people need water and rivers for?
medium.es: Piensa: ¿para qué necesitaba la gente el agua y los ríos?

label.en: “Rivers are nice to live by, and people back then probably liked the pretty views of the water.”
label.es: “Rivers are nice to live by, and people back then probably liked the pretty views of the water.”

label.en: “Towns grew along rivers because rivers gave water for farming and a way to ship goods, like cotton, to market.”
label.es: “Towns grew along rivers because rivers gave water for farming and a way to ship goods, like cotton, to market.”

label.en: “Towns grew along rivers because that is where the towns were, and towns are usually built there.”
label.es: “Towns grew along rivers because that is where the towns were, and towns are usually built there.”

why.en: “Nice” and “pretty views” are personal opinions and guesses, not historical reasons. Name what rivers provided.
why.es: “Nice” y “pretty views” son opiniones y suposiciones personales, no razones históricas. Nombra lo que proporcionaban los ríos.

hint.en: Give a specific reason, such as farming or trade.
hint.es: Da una razón específica, como la agricultura o el comercio.

why.en: Right. It gives two specific reasons (water for farming, transportation for trade) and an example (cotton).
why.es: Correcto. Da dos razones específicas (agua para la agricultura y transporte para el comercio) y un ejemplo (el algodón).

why.en: This is circular — it repeats the claim instead of explaining it.
why.es: Esto es circular: repite la afirmación en lugar de explicarla.

hint.en: A reason must add new information.
hint.es: Una razón debe agregar información nueva.

context.en: Math: A classmate says, “The mean of 2, 4, and 9 is 4, because 4 is in the middle.”
context.es: Matemáticas: Un compañero dice: “The mean of 2, 4, and 9 is 4, because 4 is in the middle.”

prompt.en: Which response evaluates the claim respectfully and with a reason?
prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta evalúa la afirmación con respeto y con una razón?

high.en: Frames: “I know ___ because ___.” / “The evidence that supports this is ___.” / “I agree / disagree with ___ because ___.”
high.es: Marcos: “I know ___ because ___.” (= “Sé que ___ porque ___”) / “The evidence that supports this is ___.” / “I agree / disagree with ___ because ___.”

medium.en: Mean = add the numbers and divide by how many there are. The middle number is the median.
medium.es: Media (mean) = suma los números y divide entre cuántos hay. El número del medio es la mediana (median).

label.en: “You're wrong, it's 5. Everybody knows that, so you should check your work next time.”
label.es: “You're wrong, it's 5. Everybody knows that, so you should check your work next time.”

label.en: “I agree. The mean is always the middle number when you put the numbers in order.”
label.es: “I agree. The mean is always the middle number when you put the numbers in order.”

label.en: “I agree that 4 is the middle number, but that is the median. The mean is (2 + 4 + 9) ÷ 3 = 5.”
label.es: “I agree that 4 is the middle number, but that is the median. The mean is (2 + 4 + 9) ÷ 3 = 5.”

why.en: The number is correct, but there is no reason, and “You're wrong… everybody knows that” is not a respectful way to evaluate.
why.es: El número es correcto, pero no hay razón, y “You're wrong… everybody knows that” no es una forma respetuosa de evaluar.

hint.en: Show the calculation and keep the tone respectful.
hint.es: Muestra el cálculo y mantén un tono respetuoso.

why.en: This repeats the mistake: the middle number of an ordered list is the median, not the mean.
why.es: Esto repite el error: el número del medio de una lista ordenada es la mediana, no la media.

hint.en: How do you calculate a mean?
hint.es: ¿Cómo se calcula la media?

why.en: Right. It agrees with the part that is true, names the confusion (median vs. mean), and shows the calculation as evidence.
why.es: Correcto. Está de acuerdo con la parte que es cierta, nombra la confusión (mediana vs. media) y muestra el cálculo como evidencia.

elps.rationale: Students justify answers and evaluate classmates' claims orally with specific reasons and evidence.
The same frames prepare students to write justifications with supporting details and evidence.

title.es: Pistas de contexto para palabras académicas

studentGoal.en: Use context clues — definition, example, contrast, cause and effect, analogy, and clues beyond the sentence — to figure out academic words in science and social studies texts.
studentGoal.es: Usa pistas de contexto —definición, ejemplo, contraste, causa y efecto, analogía y pistas fuera de la oración— para descubrir palabras académicas en textos de ciencias y estudios sociales.

studentDirections.en: Read the sentence and find the clue around the target word. Choose the meaning that fits. Choose, then select Check.
studentDirections.es: Lee la oración y encuentra la pista alrededor de la palabra meta. Elige el significado que encaja. Elige y luego selecciona Revisar.

teacherDirections.en: Each item models one context-clue type named in the grade 6–8 TEKS: definition and example (grade 6), contrast and cause-and-effect (grade 7), analogy (grade 6), and clues beyond the sentence (grade 8). Have students name the clue type (the CLEAR “lens”) and the signal words: which means, such as, unlike, because, is to. More support shows the Spanish cognate for each word — every target word has one.
teacherDirections.es: Cada ejercicio modela un tipo de pista de contexto de los TEKS de 6.º a 8.º: definición y ejemplo (6.º), contraste y causa y efecto (7.º), analogía (6.º) y pistas fuera de la oración (8.º). Pide a los estudiantes que nombren el tipo de pista (el “lente” de CLEAR) y las palabras señal: which means, such as, unlike, because, is to. Más apoyo muestra el cognado en español de cada palabra; todas las palabras meta tienen uno.

languageFunction.en: Using context clues and cognates to determine the meaning of academic vocabulary.
languageFunction.es: Usar pistas de contexto y cognados para determinar el significado del vocabulario académico.

context.en: Science: The soil in the region is arid, which means it gets very little rain and stays dry most of the year.
context.es: Ciencias: The soil in the region is arid, which means it gets very little rain and stays dry most of the year.

prompt.en: What does “arid” mean here?

high.en: Clue type: definition (“which means”). Spanish cognate: árido.
high.es: Tipo de pista: definición (“which means” = “lo que significa”). Cognado en español: árido.

medium.en: Read the words right after “which means.”
medium.es: Lee las palabras justo después de “which means.”

label.en: very wet
label.es: muy húmedo

label.en: very dry
label.es: muy seco

label.en: very rocky
label.es: muy rocoso

why.en: The sentence says the soil gets very little rain and stays dry — the opposite of wet.
why.es: La oración dice que el suelo recibe muy poca lluvia y se mantiene seco: lo contrario de húmedo.

hint.en: What does the sentence say after “which means”?
hint.es: ¿Qué dice la oración después de “which means”?

why.en: Right. “Which means” signals a definition: little rain, dry most of the year. Arid = árido.
why.es: Correcto. “Which means” señala una definición: poca lluvia, seco casi todo el año. Arid = árido.

why.en: Nothing in the sentence mentions rocks. The definition clue is about rain and dryness.
why.es: Nada en la oración menciona rocas. La pista de definición trata de la lluvia y la sequedad.

hint.en: Use only what the sentence tells you.
hint.es: Usa solo lo que te dice la oración.

context.en: Science: Herbivores, such as deer, rabbits, and cows, eat only plants.
context.es: Ciencias: Herbivores, such as deer, rabbits, and cows, eat only plants.

prompt.en: What are “herbivores”?

high.en: Clue type: example (“such as”). Spanish cognate: herbívoros.
high.es: Tipo de pista: ejemplo (“such as” = “como”). Cognado en español: herbívoros.

medium.en: What do deer, rabbits, and cows have in common?
medium.es: ¿Qué tienen en común los venados, los conejos y las vacas?

label.en: animals that eat other animals
label.es: animales que comen otros animales

label.en: animals that live on farms
label.es: animales que viven en granjas

label.en: animals that eat only plants
label.es: animales que solo comen plantas

why.en: Deer, rabbits, and cows do not eat other animals, and the sentence says “eat only plants.”
why.es: Los venados, los conejos y las vacas no comen otros animales, y la oración dice “eat only plants.”

hint.en: Look at the examples and the end of the sentence.
hint.es: Mira los ejemplos y el final de la oración.

why.en: Cows live on farms, but deer and rabbits usually live in the wild. The examples share their diet, not where they live.
why.es: Las vacas viven en granjas, pero los venados y los conejos suelen vivir en la naturaleza. Los ejemplos comparten su dieta, no dónde viven.

hint.en: What do ALL three examples share?
hint.es: ¿Qué comparten LOS TRES ejemplos?

why.en: Right. “Such as” introduces examples, and all three eat only plants. Herbivores = herbívoros.
why.es: Correcto. “Such as” introduce ejemplos, y los tres comen solo plantas. Herbivores = herbívoros.

context.en: Science: Unlike clear glass, which lets light pass through, the wooden door is opaque.
context.es: Ciencias: Unlike clear glass, which lets light pass through, the wooden door is opaque.

prompt.en: What does “opaque” mean here?

high.en: Clue type: contrast (“unlike”). Spanish cognate: opaco.
high.es: Tipo de pista: contraste (“unlike” = “a diferencia de”). Cognado en español: opaco.

medium.en: “Unlike” tells you the door is the OPPOSITE of clear glass.
medium.es: “Unlike” te dice que la puerta es lo CONTRARIO del vidrio transparente.

label.en: does not let light pass through
label.es: no deja pasar la luz

label.en: shiny, smooth, and hard to scratch
label.es: brillante, liso y difícil de rayar

label.en: easy to break
label.es: fácil de romper

why.en: Right. “Unlike” signals contrast: glass lets light through, so the opaque door does not. Opaque = opaco.
why.es: Correcto. “Unlike” señala un contraste: el vidrio deja pasar la luz, así que la puerta opaca no. Opaque = opaco.

why.en: The contrast is about light passing through, not about how the surface looks or feels.
why.es: El contraste trata de si pasa la luz, no de cómo se ve o se siente la superficie.

hint.en: What does glass do that the door does not?
hint.es: ¿Qué hace el vidrio que la puerta no hace?

why.en: Glass breaks easily, but the sentence contrasts the two by light, not by strength.
why.es: El vidrio se rompe fácilmente, pero la oración los contrasta por la luz, no por la resistencia.

hint.en: Find the words after “which.”
hint.es: Busca las palabras después de “which.”

context.en: Social studies: Because the old bridge was unstable, engineers closed it until it could be repaired.
context.es: Estudios sociales: Because the old bridge was unstable, engineers closed it until it could be repaired.

prompt.en: What does “unstable” mean here?

high.en: Clue type: cause and effect (“because”). Spanish cognate: inestable.
high.es: Tipo de pista: causa y efecto (“because” = “porque”). Cognado en español: inestable.

medium.en: The effect is that engineers closed the bridge. What cause would make them do that?
medium.es: El efecto es que los ingenieros cerraron el puente. ¿Qué causa los llevaría a hacer eso?

label.en: brand new and recently painted
label.es: completamente nuevo y recién pintado

label.en: not firm; likely to move or fall
label.es: poco firme; que puede moverse o caerse

label.en: too crowded with cars and people
label.es: demasiado lleno de carros y gente

why.en: A brand-new, freshly painted bridge would not need repairs. The sentence says it was old and needed fixing.
why.es: Un puente nuevo y recién pintado no necesitaría reparaciones. La oración dice que era viejo y había que arreglarlo.

hint.en: Why would engineers close a bridge to repair it?
hint.es: ¿Por qué cerrarían los ingenieros un puente para repararlo?

why.en: Right. “Because” links cause and effect: the bridge was not firm, so it was closed for repair. Unstable = inestable (un- = in-, “not”).
why.es: Correcto. “Because” une causa y efecto: el puente no era firme, así que lo cerraron para repararlo. Unstable = inestable (un- = in-, “no”).

why.en: Crowding is not fixed by repairs. The clue “until it could be repaired” points to a problem with the bridge itself.
why.es: La cantidad de carros y gente no se arregla con reparaciones. La pista “until it could be repaired” apunta a un problema del puente mismo.

hint.en: Notice “until it could be repaired.”
hint.es: Fíjate en “until it could be repaired.”

context.en: Social studies: A tributary is to a river as a branch is to a tree trunk.
context.es: Estudios sociales: A tributary is to a river as a branch is to a tree trunk.

prompt.en: What is a “tributary”?

high.en: Clue type: analogy (“is to … as … is to”). Spanish: afluente or río tributario.
high.es: Tipo de pista: analogía (“is to … as … is to”). En español: afluente o río tributario.

medium.en: A branch is a smaller part that joins the trunk. Apply that to a river.
medium.es: Una rama es una parte más pequeña que se une al tronco. Aplica eso a un río.

label.en: a smaller stream that flows into a larger river
label.es: un arroyo más pequeño que desemboca en un río más grande

label.en: the place where a river meets the ocean
label.es: el lugar donde un río llega al océano

label.en: a wall built across a river
label.es: un muro construido a lo ancho de un río

why.en: Right. A branch joins a trunk the way a smaller stream joins a larger river. Tributary = tributario / afluente.
why.es: Correcto. Una rama se une al tronco como un arroyo más pequeño se une a un río más grande. Tributary = tributario / afluente.

why.en: That is a river's mouth (desembocadura). The analogy compares a smaller part joining a bigger one, like a branch and a trunk.
why.es: Eso es la desembocadura de un río. La analogía compara una parte pequeña que se une a una más grande, como una rama y un tronco.

hint.en: How does a branch relate to a trunk?
hint.es: ¿Qué relación tiene una rama con el tronco?

why.en: That is a dam (presa). A branch is a natural part that connects to the trunk, not something built to block it.
why.es: Eso es una presa (dam). Una rama es una parte natural que se conecta al tronco, no algo construido para bloquearlo.

hint.en: Follow the analogy: branch → trunk.
hint.es: Sigue la analogía: rama → tronco.

context.en: Social studies: The colonists refused to buy British tea. The boycott lasted for months, and merchants in London lost a great deal of money.
context.es: Estudios sociales: The colonists refused to buy British tea. The boycott lasted for months, and merchants in London lost a great deal of money.

prompt.en: What is a “boycott”?

high.en: Clue type: beyond the sentence — read the sentence BEFORE the word. Spanish cognate: boicot.
high.es: Tipo de pista: fuera de la oración; lee la oración ANTERIOR a la palabra. Cognado en español: boicot.

medium.en: “The boycott” refers back to something in the first sentence.
medium.es: “The boycott” se refiere a algo de la primera oración.

label.en: a tax on imported goods
label.es: un impuesto sobre productos importados

label.en: a trade agreement between two countries
label.es: un acuerdo comercial entre dos países

label.en: refusing to buy something as a form of protest
label.es: negarse a comprar algo como forma de protesta

why.en: A tax would make merchants collect money, not lose it. The first sentence says the colonists refused to buy.
why.es: Un impuesto haría que se cobrara dinero, no que se perdiera. La primera oración dice que los colonos se negaron a comprar.

hint.en: Reread the first sentence.
hint.es: Vuelve a leer la primera oración.

why.en: An agreement means both sides cooperate. Here the colonists refused to buy, and London merchants lost money.
why.es: Un acuerdo significa que ambos lados cooperan. Aquí los colonos se negaron a comprar, y los comerciantes de Londres perdieron dinero.

hint.en: What did the colonists refuse to do?
hint.es: ¿Qué se negaron a hacer los colonos?

why.en: Right. “The boycott” points back to the colonists refusing to buy tea, and the next clause shows its effect. Boycott = boicot.
why.es: Correcto. “The boycott” se refiere a que los colonos se negaron a comprar té, y lo que sigue muestra su efecto. Boycott = boicot.

elps.rationale: Students use contextual factors and cognates to comprehend content-area vocabulary in text.

teks.rationale: Students use definition, example, and analogy clues to clarify the meaning of academic words.
Students use contrast and cause-and-effect clues to clarify the meaning of academic words.
Students use context within and beyond a sentence to clarify unfamiliar academic words.

title.en: Talk Like a Mathematician, Scientist, or Historian
title.es: Habla como matemático, científico o historiador

studentGoal.en: Recognize and use the discussion language of each content area — how mathematicians, scientists, and historians talk about their thinking.
studentGoal.es: Reconoce y usa el lenguaje de discusión de cada materia: cómo hablan de su razonamiento los matemáticos, los científicos y los historiadores.

studentDirections.en: Read each discussion sentence. Decide which class you would most likely hear it in: math, science, or social studies. Place each sentence, then select Check.
studentDirections.es: Lee cada oración de discusión. Decide en qué clase es más probable escucharla: matemáticas, ciencias o estudios sociales. Coloca cada oración y luego selecciona Revisar.

teacherDirections.en: Each content area has its own ways of talking: mathematicians represent and check, scientists hypothesize and infer, historians cite sources and weigh perspectives. After sorting, have students choose one sentence from each bin, turn it into a frame (“According to this primary source, ___”), and say it aloud in their next discussion in that class. Many of the key words have Spanish cognates (hipótesis, variable, perspectiva, fuente primaria) — More support shows them.
teacherDirections.es: Cada materia tiene su propia forma de hablar: los matemáticos representan y comprueban, los científicos plantean hipótesis e infieren, los historiadores citan fuentes y consideran perspectivas. Después de clasificar, pide a los estudiantes que elijan una oración de cada categoría, la conviertan en un marco (“According to this primary source, ___”) y la digan en voz alta en su próxima discusión en esa clase. Muchas palabras clave tienen cognados en español (hipótesis, variable, perspectiva, fuente primaria); Más apoyo los muestra.

languageFunction.en: Classifying and rehearsing discipline-specific discussion language.
languageFunction.es: Clasificar y practicar el lenguaje de discusión propio de cada materia.

label.en: Math talk
label.es: Lenguaje de matemáticas

hint.en: Equations, representations, patterns, and checking answers.
hint.es: Ecuaciones, representaciones, patrones y comprobar respuestas.

label.en: Science talk
label.es: Lenguaje de ciencias

hint.en: Hypotheses, variables, observations, and data.
hint.es: Hipótesis, variables, observaciones y datos.

label.en: Social studies talk
label.es: Lenguaje de estudios sociales

hint.en: Sources, causes and effects, and perspectives.
hint.es: Fuentes, causas y efectos, y perspectivas.

prompt.en: “I can check my answer by substituting it back into the equation.”
prompt.es: “I can check my answer by substituting it back into the equation.”

high.en: Spanish: “Puedo comprobar mi respuesta sustituyéndola en la ecuación.”
high.es: “Puedo comprobar mi respuesta sustituyéndola en la ecuación.”

medium.en: Key words: substituting, equation.
medium.es: Palabras clave: substituting (sustituir), equation (ecuación).

why.en: Substituting a value back into an equation is how mathematicians check a solution.
why.es: Sustituir un valor en una ecuación es la manera en que los matemáticos comprueban una solución.

hint.en: Which subject checks answers with equations and patterns?
hint.es: ¿Qué materia comprueba respuestas con ecuaciones y patrones?

prompt.en: “Our hypothesis was that plants grow taller with more light, and the data supported it.”
prompt.es: “Our hypothesis was that plants grow taller with more light, and the data supported it.”

high.en: Spanish: “Nuestra hipótesis era que las plantas crecen más con más luz, y los datos la apoyaron.”
high.es: “Nuestra hipótesis era que las plantas crecen más con más luz, y los datos la apoyaron.”

medium.en: Key words: hypothesis, data.
medium.es: Palabras clave: hypothesis (hipótesis), data (datos).

why.en: Stating a hypothesis and whether the data supported it is core science discussion language.
why.es: Expresar una hipótesis y si los datos la apoyaron es lenguaje central de las discusiones de ciencias.

hint.en: Which subject tests hypotheses and collects data?
hint.es: ¿Qué materia pone a prueba hipótesis y recoge datos?

prompt.en: “According to this primary source, the settlers were worried about a shortage of food.”
prompt.es: “According to this primary source, the settlers were worried about a shortage of food.”

high.en: Spanish: “Según esta fuente primaria, los colonos estaban preocupados por la escasez de comida.”
high.es: “Según esta fuente primaria, los colonos estaban preocupados por la escasez de comida.”

medium.en: Key words: primary source.
medium.es: Palabras clave: primary source (fuente primaria).

why.en: Historians cite primary sources — documents from the time — to support what they say about the past.
why.es: Los historiadores citan fuentes primarias (documentos de la época) para apoyar lo que dicen sobre el pasado.

hint.en: Which subject studies sources, causes, and perspectives in history?
hint.es: ¿Qué materia estudia fuentes, causas y perspectivas en la historia?

prompt.en: “Another way to represent this relationship is with a table of values.”
prompt.es: “Another way to represent this relationship is with a table of values.”

high.en: Spanish: “Otra manera de representar esta relación es con una tabla de valores.”
high.es: “Otra manera de representar esta relación es con una tabla de valores.”

medium.en: Key words: represent, table of values.
medium.es: Palabras clave: represent (representar), table of values (tabla de valores).

why.en: Showing the same relationship with a table, graph, or equation is a key move in math discussion.
why.es: Mostrar la misma relación con una tabla, una gráfica o una ecuación es un movimiento clave en las discusiones de matemáticas.

hint.en: Which subject checks answers with equations and patterns?
hint.es: ¿Qué materia comprueba respuestas con ecuaciones y patrones?

prompt.en: “The independent variable in our investigation was the temperature of the water.”
prompt.es: “The independent variable in our investigation was the temperature of the water.”

high.en: Spanish: “La variable independiente de nuestra investigación fue la temperatura del agua.”
high.es: “La variable independiente de nuestra investigación fue la temperatura del agua.”

medium.en: Key words: independent variable, investigation.
medium.es: Palabras clave: independent variable (variable independiente), investigation (investigación).

why.en: The independent variable is the factor a scientist changes on purpose in an investigation.
why.es: La variable independiente es el factor que un científico cambia a propósito en una investigación.

hint.en: Which subject tests hypotheses and collects data?
hint.es: ¿Qué materia pone a prueba hipótesis y recoge datos?

prompt.en: “One cause of the conflict was competition for land, and one effect was a new treaty.”
prompt.es: “One cause of the conflict was competition for land, and one effect was a new treaty.”

high.en: Spanish: “Una causa del conflicto fue la competencia por la tierra, y un efecto fue un nuevo tratado.”
high.es: “Una causa del conflicto fue la competencia por la tierra, y un efecto fue un nuevo tratado.”

medium.en: Key words: cause, conflict, effect, treaty.
medium.es: Palabras clave: cause (causa), conflict (conflicto), effect (efecto), treaty (tratado).

why.en: Explaining the causes and effects of historical events, such as conflicts and treaties, is social studies reasoning.
why.es: Explicar las causas y los efectos de sucesos históricos, como conflictos y tratados, es razonamiento de estudios sociales.

hint.en: Which subject studies sources, causes, and perspectives in history?
hint.es: ¿Qué materia estudia fuentes, causas y perspectivas en la historia?

prompt.en: “The pattern increases by 4 each time, so the rule is y = 4x.”
prompt.es: “The pattern increases by 4 each time, so the rule is y = 4x.”

high.en: Spanish: “El patrón aumenta de 4 en 4, así que la regla es y = 4x.”
high.es: “El patrón aumenta de 4 en 4, así que la regla es y = 4x.”

medium.en: Key words: pattern, rule.
medium.es: Palabras clave: pattern (patrón), rule (regla).

why.en: Describing a pattern and writing its rule as an equation is algebraic thinking.
why.es: Describir un patrón y escribir su regla como ecuación es pensamiento algebraico.

hint.en: Which subject checks answers with equations and patterns?
hint.es: ¿Qué materia comprueba respuestas con ecuaciones y patrones?

prompt.en: “We observed bubbles forming, so we can infer that a gas was produced.”
prompt.es: “We observed bubbles forming, so we can infer that a gas was produced.”

high.en: Spanish: “Observamos que se formaban burbujas, así que podemos inferir que se produjo un gas.”
high.es: “Observamos que se formaban burbujas, así que podemos inferir que se produjo un gas.”

medium.en: Key words: observed, infer.
medium.es: Palabras clave: observed (observamos), infer (inferir).

why.en: Moving from an observation to an inference is how scientists reason from evidence in a lab.
why.es: Pasar de una observación a una inferencia es la manera en que los científicos razonan a partir de la evidencia en el laboratorio.

hint.en: Which subject tests hypotheses and collects data?
hint.es: ¿Qué materia pone a prueba hipótesis y recoge datos?

prompt.en: “From the perspective of the farmers, the new railroad meant they could sell crops in distant cities.”
prompt.es: “From the perspective of the farmers, the new railroad meant they could sell crops in distant cities.”

high.en: Spanish: “Desde la perspectiva de los agricultores, el nuevo ferrocarril significaba que podían vender sus cosechas en ciudades lejanas.”
high.es: “Desde la perspectiva de los agricultores, el nuevo ferrocarril significaba que podían vender sus cosechas en ciudades lejanas.”

medium.en: Key words: perspective.
medium.es: Palabras clave: perspective (perspectiva).

why.en: Considering how a historical event looked to different groups — their perspective — is social studies thinking.
why.es: Considerar cómo vieron un suceso histórico distintos grupos (su perspectiva) es pensamiento de estudios sociales.

hint.en: Which subject studies sources, causes, and perspectives in history?
hint.es: ¿Qué materia estudia fuentes, causas y perspectivas en la historia?

elps.rationale: Students sort and then say aloud discussion sentences built on each content area's academic vocabulary.
The sorted sentences are frames for explaining and justifying in math, science, and social studies discussions.

studentGoal.en: Choose the transition word that shows how two ideas connect — cause and effect, example, contrast, sequence, or comparison — in a written explanation.
studentGoal.es: Elige la palabra de transición que muestra cómo se conectan dos ideas —causa y efecto, ejemplo, contraste, secuencia o comparación— en una explicación escrita.

studentDirections.en: Read the two sentences. Decide how the second idea connects to the first, then choose the transition that fits the blank. Choose, then select Check.
studentDirections.es: Lee las dos oraciones. Decide cómo se conecta la segunda idea con la primera y elige la transición que completa el espacio. Elige y luego selecciona Revisar.

teacherDirections.en: Transitions are not interchangeable: each one signals a relationship. Before choosing, have students name the relationship (cause/effect, example, contrast, sequence, comparison). The distractors are real transitions that signal the wrong relationship. Extend by having students write a three-sentence explanation in their current science or social studies unit using two transitions from the bank.
teacherDirections.es: Las transiciones no son intercambiables: cada una señala una relación. Antes de elegir, pide a los estudiantes que nombren la relación (causa/efecto, ejemplo, contraste, secuencia, comparación). Los distractores son transiciones reales que señalan la relación equivocada. Para ampliar, pide que escriban una explicación de tres oraciones sobre su unidad actual de ciencias o estudios sociales usando dos transiciones del banco.

languageFunction.en: Connecting ideas in written explanations with transitions that signal relationships.
languageFunction.es: Conectar ideas en explicaciones escritas con transiciones que señalan relaciones.

context.en: Science: “Plants need sunlight to make their own food. ___, a plant kept in a dark closet for weeks will grow weak.”
context.es: Ciencias: “Plants need sunlight to make their own food. ___, a plant kept in a dark closet for weeks will grow weak.”

prompt.en: Which transition fits the blank?

high.en: Transition bank: as a result (cause → effect) · for example (example) · however (contrast) · next (sequence) · similarly (comparison).
high.es: Banco de transiciones: as a result (= como resultado; causa → efecto) · for example (= por ejemplo) · however (= sin embargo; contraste) · next (= luego; secuencia) · similarly (= de manera similar; comparación).

medium.en: Is the second sentence a result of the first?
medium.es: ¿La segunda oración es un resultado de la primera?

label.en: However
label.es: However

label.en: For example
label.es: For example

label.en: As a result
label.es: As a result

why.en: “However” signals a contrast, but the second sentence does not contradict the first — it follows from it.
why.es: “However” señala un contraste, pero la segunda oración no contradice la primera: es una consecuencia de ella.

hint.en: Is this a contrast or a result?
hint.es: ¿Es un contraste o un resultado?

why.en: A plant growing weak is not an example of needing sunlight; it is what happens without it.
why.es: Que una planta se debilite no es un ejemplo de necesitar luz; es lo que pasa sin ella.

hint.en: Look for a cause-and-effect transition.
hint.es: Busca una transición de causa y efecto.

why.en: Right. No sunlight (cause) → weak plant (effect). “As a result” signals cause and effect.
why.es: Correcto. Sin luz solar (causa) → planta débil (efecto). “As a result” señala causa y efecto.

context.en: Science: “Many animals have adaptations for cold climates. ___, the arctic fox grows a thick white coat in winter.”
context.es: Ciencias: “Many animals have adaptations for cold climates. ___, the arctic fox grows a thick white coat in winter.”

prompt.en: Which transition fits the blank?

high.en: Transition bank: as a result (cause → effect) · for example (example) · however (contrast) · next (sequence) · similarly (comparison).
high.es: Banco de transiciones: as a result (= como resultado; causa → efecto) · for example (= por ejemplo) · however (= sin embargo; contraste) · next (= luego; secuencia) · similarly (= de manera similar; comparación).

medium.en: Is the arctic fox one case of the general idea?
medium.es: ¿El zorro ártico es un caso de la idea general?

label.en: For example
label.es: For example

label.en: Instead
label.es: Instead

label.en: In conclusion
label.es: In conclusion

why.en: Right. The first sentence is general; the arctic fox is a specific case. “For example” introduces it.
why.es: Correcto. La primera oración es general; el zorro ártico es un caso específico. “For example” lo introduce.

why.en: “Instead” signals a replacement, but the fox does not replace the first idea — it illustrates it.
why.es: “Instead” señala un reemplazo, pero el zorro no reemplaza la primera idea: la ilustra.

hint.en: General idea → specific case. Which transition fits?
hint.es: Idea general → caso específico. ¿Qué transición encaja?

why.en: “In conclusion” wraps up a whole explanation. Here the writer is just starting to give a specific case.
why.es: “In conclusion” cierra toda una explicación. Aquí el autor apenas empieza a dar un caso específico.

hint.en: The second sentence gives one case.
hint.es: La segunda oración da un caso.

context.en: Social studies: “Spanish explorers came to Texas hoping to find gold. ___, they found few riches and faced many hardships.”
context.es: Estudios sociales: “Spanish explorers came to Texas hoping to find gold. ___, they found few riches and faced many hardships.”

prompt.en: Which transition fits the blank?

high.en: Transition bank: as a result (cause → effect) · for example (example) · however (contrast) · next (sequence) · similarly (comparison).
high.es: Banco de transiciones: as a result (= como resultado; causa → efecto) · for example (= por ejemplo) · however (= sin embargo; contraste) · next (= luego; secuencia) · similarly (= de manera similar; comparación).

medium.en: What they hoped for and what happened are different.
medium.es: Lo que esperaban y lo que pasó son diferentes.

label.en: Therefore
label.es: Therefore

label.en: However
label.es: However

label.en: Similarly
label.es: Similarly

why.en: “Therefore” signals a result, but hoping for gold did not cause them to find little. The ideas contrast.
why.es: “Therefore” señala un resultado, pero esperar oro no causó que encontraran poco. Las ideas contrastan.

hint.en: Hope vs. reality — what relationship is that?
hint.es: Expectativa vs. realidad: ¿qué relación es esa?

why.en: Right. What they expected (gold) contrasts with what happened (few riches). “However” signals that contrast.
why.es: Correcto. Lo que esperaban (oro) contrasta con lo que pasó (pocas riquezas). “However” señala ese contraste.

why.en: “Similarly” signals that two things are alike, but these ideas are opposites.
why.es: “Similarly” señala que dos cosas se parecen, pero estas ideas son opuestas.

hint.en: Are the two ideas alike or different?
hint.es: ¿Las dos ideas se parecen o son diferentes?

context.en: Math: “To find the area of a rectangle, first measure the length and the width. ___, multiply the length by the width.”
context.es: Matemáticas: “To find the area of a rectangle, first measure the length and the width. ___, multiply the length by the width.”

prompt.en: Which transition fits the blank?

high.en: Transition bank: as a result (cause → effect) · for example (example) · however (contrast) · next (sequence) · similarly (comparison).
high.es: Banco de transiciones: as a result (= como resultado; causa → efecto) · for example (= por ejemplo) · however (= sin embargo; contraste) · next (= luego; secuencia) · similarly (= de manera similar; comparación).

medium.en: The first sentence says “first.” What comes after first?
medium.es: La primera oración dice “first”. ¿Qué viene después de “first”?

label.en: Although
label.es: Although

label.en: For instance
label.es: For instance

label.en: Next
label.es: Next

why.en: “Although” introduces a contrast, but these are steps in order.
why.es: “Although” introduce un contraste, pero estos son pasos en orden.

hint.en: Look for a sequence word.
hint.es: Busca una palabra de secuencia.

why.en: “For instance” introduces an example, but multiplying is the next step, not an example.
why.es: “For instance” introduce un ejemplo, pero multiplicar es el siguiente paso, no un ejemplo.

hint.en: These are steps. Which word shows order?
hint.es: Son pasos. ¿Qué palabra muestra el orden?

why.en: Right. “First … next” shows the order of steps in a procedure.
why.es: Correcto. “First … next” muestra el orden de los pasos de un procedimiento.

context.en: Math: “The mean is one way to describe the center of a data set. ___, the median also describes the center of a data set.”
context.es: Matemáticas: “The mean is one way to describe the center of a data set. ___, the median also describes the center of a data set.”

prompt.en: Which transition fits the blank?

high.en: Transition bank: as a result (cause → effect) · for example (example) · however (contrast) · next (sequence) · similarly (comparison).
high.es: Banco de transiciones: as a result (= como resultado; causa → efecto) · for example (= por ejemplo) · however (= sin embargo; contraste) · next (= luego; secuencia) · similarly (= de manera similar; comparación).

medium.en: Both sentences say the same kind of thing about two measures.
medium.es: Las dos oraciones dicen lo mismo sobre dos medidas.

label.en: As a result
label.es: As a result

label.en: Similarly
label.es: Similarly

label.en: Otherwise
label.es: Otherwise

why.en: The median does not describe the center BECAUSE of the mean. There is no cause and effect here.
why.es: La mediana no describe el centro POR CAUSA de la media. Aquí no hay causa y efecto.

hint.en: Are the two measures being compared?
hint.es: ¿Se están comparando las dos medidas?

why.en: Right. Both the mean and the median describe the center, so “Similarly” signals the comparison.
why.es: Correcto. Tanto la media como la mediana describen el centro, así que “Similarly” señala la comparación.

why.en: “Otherwise” means “if not,” which does not connect these two ideas.
why.es: “Otherwise” significa “si no”, lo cual no conecta estas dos ideas.

hint.en: Notice the word “also.”
hint.es: Fíjate en la palabra “also.”

elps.rationale: Students choose transition words that signal cause, example, contrast, sequence, and comparison in written content-area explanations.
Students can use the same transition words when explaining their thinking aloud.

title.es: Revisa para usar un registro académico

studentGoal.en: Revise sentences in your own academic responses so the register, vocabulary, and tone fit an essay, lab report, or constructed response — without sounding stiff or inflated.
studentGoal.es: Revisa oraciones de tus propias respuestas académicas para que el registro, el vocabulario y el tono sean adecuados para un ensayo, un informe de laboratorio o una respuesta construida, sin sonar rígido ni rebuscado.

studentDirections.en: Each item shows a draft sentence from a student's academic response. Choose the best revision. Choose, then select Check.
studentDirections.es: Cada ejercicio muestra una oración en borrador de la respuesta académica de un estudiante. Elige la mejor revisión. Elige y luego selecciona Revisar.

teacherDirections.en: This activity follows “Formal or Informal?”: there students matched register to a situation; here every item is already an academic response, and the work is revising inside it. Each item targets one habit: vague “I think … kinda,” second-person “you,” slang and contractions, emotional tone in a lab report, and dismissing a counterargument. Note the inflated distractors — academic register is precise, not pompous. Have students apply the same moves to a paragraph from their own recent writing.
teacherDirections.es: Esta actividad sigue a “Formal or Informal?”: allí los estudiantes adaptaban el registro a una situación; aquí cada ejercicio ya es una respuesta académica, y el trabajo es revisar dentro de ella. Cada ejercicio trata un hábito: el vago “I think … kinda”, la segunda persona “you”, la jerga y las contracciones, el tono emotivo en un informe de laboratorio y el rechazo de un contraargumento. Fíjate en los distractores rebuscados: el registro académico es preciso, no pomposo. Pide a los estudiantes que apliquen los mismos cambios a un párrafo de su propia escritura reciente.

languageFunction.en: Revising academic writing for appropriate register, vocabulary, tone, and voice.
languageFunction.es: Revisar la escritura académica para lograr un registro, vocabulario, tono y voz apropiados.

context.en: Short constructed response about a poem. Draft: “I think the poem is kinda sad.”
context.es: Respuesta construida corta sobre un poema. Borrador: “I think the poem is kinda sad.”

prompt.en: Which revision fits an academic response?
prompt.es: ¿Qué revisión es adecuada para una respuesta académica?

high.en: Name the device and the effect: “The poem's ___ creates a ___ tone.” / Nombra el recurso y su efecto.
high.es: Nombra el recurso y su efecto: “The poem's ___ creates a ___ tone.”

medium.en: Replace “kinda sad” with a precise tone word and point to the text.
medium.es: Cambia “kinda sad” por una palabra de tono precisa y señala el texto.

label.en: “The poem is super depressing, not gonna lie.”
label.es: “The poem is super depressing, not gonna lie.”

label.en: “The poem's images of empty rooms create a mournful tone.”
label.es: “The poem's images of empty rooms create a mournful tone.”

label.en: “In my own humble and personal opinion, the poem is perhaps somewhat sad in a certain way.”
label.es: “In my own humble and personal opinion, the poem is perhaps somewhat sad in a certain way.”

why.en: “Super” and “not gonna lie” are conversational slang, and the sentence still gives no evidence from the poem.
why.es: “Super” y “not gonna lie” son jerga conversacional, y la oración sigue sin dar evidencia del poema.

hint.en: Which choice names something in the poem?
hint.es: ¿Qué opción nombra algo del poema?

why.en: Right. “Mournful” is a precise tone word, and “images of empty rooms” points to evidence in the text.
why.es: Correcto. “Mournful” es una palabra de tono precisa, e “images of empty rooms” señala evidencia del texto.

why.en: More words do not make it more academic. Piling up “humble,” “personal,” “perhaps,” and “somewhat” makes the point weaker, not more formal.
why.es: Más palabras no lo hacen más académico. Acumular “humble”, “personal”, “perhaps” y “somewhat” debilita la idea, no la hace más formal.

hint.en: Academic means precise, not wordy.
hint.es: Académico significa preciso, no palabrero.

context.en: Article analysis. Draft: “When you read the article, you can tell the author doesn't trust the company.”
context.es: Análisis de un artículo. Borrador: “When you read the article, you can tell the author doesn't trust the company.”

prompt.en: Which revision fits an academic response?
prompt.es: ¿Qué revisión es adecuada para una respuesta académica?

high.en: Avoid “you.” Make the author or the text the subject: “The author's use of ___ signals ___.”
high.es: Evita “you”. Haz que el autor o el texto sea el sujeto: “The author's use of ___ signals ___.”

medium.en: Who is the sentence about — the reader or the author?
medium.es: ¿De quién trata la oración: del lector o del autor?

label.en: “The author's repeated use of the word ‘claims’ signals distrust of the company.”
label.es: “The author's repeated use of the word ‘claims’ signals distrust of the company.”

label.en: “You can totally tell the author hates the company.”
label.es: “You can totally tell the author hates the company.”

label.en: “As you, the reader, will surely agree, you can tell the author doesn't trust them.”
label.es: “As you, the reader, will surely agree, you can tell the author doesn't trust them.”

why.en: Right. The author becomes the subject, “you” disappears, and the word choice “claims” is the evidence for the inference.
why.es: Correcto. El autor pasa a ser el sujeto, desaparece “you” y la palabra “claims” es la evidencia de la inferencia.

why.en: “You,” “totally,” and “hates” keep the casual register and exaggerate the author's attitude.
why.es: “You”, “totally” y “hates” mantienen el registro casual y exageran la actitud del autor.

hint.en: Remove “you” and point to the author's words.
hint.es: Quita “you” y señala las palabras del autor.

why.en: This sounds more formal but uses “you” three times and assumes the reader agrees instead of showing evidence.
why.es: Esto suena más formal, pero usa “you” tres veces y supone que el lector está de acuerdo en lugar de mostrar evidencia.

hint.en: Make the author the subject.
hint.es: Haz que el autor sea el sujeto.

context.en: History short answer. Draft: “The treaty didn't work out ’cause neither side trusted the other.”
context.es: Respuesta corta de historia. Borrador: “The treaty didn't work out ’cause neither side trusted the other.”

prompt.en: Which revision fits an academic response?
prompt.es: ¿Qué revisión es adecuada para una respuesta académica?

high.en: Swap the casual words: “didn't work out” → “failed”; “’cause” → “because.”
high.es: Cambia las palabras casuales: “didn't work out” → “failed” (fracasó); “’cause” → “because” (porque).

medium.en: Keep the idea; change only the casual words.
medium.es: Mantén la idea; cambia solo las palabras casuales.

label.en: “The treaty was a total flop.”
label.es: “The treaty was a total flop.”

label.en: “The aforementioned treaty was rendered ineffectual by virtue of the mutual and reciprocal absence of trust.”
label.es: “The aforementioned treaty was rendered ineffectual by virtue of the mutual and reciprocal absence of trust.”

label.en: “The treaty failed because neither side trusted the other.”
label.es: “The treaty failed because neither side trusted the other.”

why.en: “A total flop” is slang, and the sentence drops the reason (lack of trust).
why.es: “A total flop” es jerga, y la oración elimina la razón (la falta de confianza).

hint.en: Keep the reason and use precise words.
hint.es: Mantén la razón y usa palabras precisas.

why.en: This is inflated: “aforementioned,” “rendered ineffectual,” and “mutual and reciprocal” (which repeat each other) make a simple idea hard to read.
why.es: Esto es rebuscado: “aforementioned”, “rendered ineffectual” y “mutual and reciprocal” (que se repiten) hacen difícil de leer una idea sencilla.

hint.en: Clear and precise beats long and fancy.
hint.es: Claro y preciso es mejor que largo y elegante.

why.en: Right. “Failed” and “because” replace the casual words, and the sentence stays clear and direct.
why.es: Correcto. “Failed” y “because” reemplazan las palabras casuales, y la oración queda clara y directa.

context.en: Lab report conclusion. Draft: “Our experiment was a fail, lol, the plant died.”
context.es: Conclusión de un informe de laboratorio. Borrador: “Our experiment was a fail, lol, the plant died.”

prompt.en: Which revision fits a lab report?
prompt.es: ¿Qué revisión es adecuada para un informe de laboratorio?

high.en: Lab reports state results objectively: “The results did / did not support our hypothesis; ___.”
high.es: Los informes de laboratorio presentan los resultados con objetividad: “The results did / did not support our hypothesis; ___.”

medium.en: Report what happened and connect it to the hypothesis, without emotion.
medium.es: Informa lo que pasó y relaciónalo con la hipótesis, sin emoción.

label.en: “Sadly, our poor little plant in the saltwater group tragically passed away by day five.”
label.es: “Sadly, our poor little plant in the saltwater group tragically passed away by day five.”

label.en: “The results did not support our hypothesis; the plant in the saltwater group died by day five.”
label.es: “The results did not support our hypothesis; the plant in the saltwater group died by day five.”

label.en: “The plant died. Oh well.”
label.es: “The plant died. Oh well.”

why.en: “Sadly,” “poor little,” and “tragically passed away” add emotional tone, and the result is never linked to the hypothesis. A lab report reports results objectively.
why.es: “Sadly”, “poor little” y “tragically passed away” agregan un tono emotivo, y el resultado nunca se relaciona con la hipótesis. Un informe de laboratorio presenta los resultados con objetividad.

hint.en: Remove the feelings; keep the data.
hint.es: Quita los sentimientos; mantén los datos.

why.en: Right. It connects the result to the hypothesis and gives specific data (saltwater group, day five) in an objective tone.
why.es: Correcto. Relaciona el resultado con la hipótesis y da datos específicos (grupo con agua salada, día cinco) con un tono objetivo.

why.en: “Oh well” is casual, and the sentence gives no data or link to the hypothesis.
why.es: “Oh well” es casual, y la oración no da datos ni relación con la hipótesis.

hint.en: Which choice mentions the hypothesis?
hint.es: ¿Qué opción menciona la hipótesis?

context.en: Argument essay. Draft: “People who disagree with me are just wrong.”
context.es: Ensayo argumentativo. Borrador: “People who disagree with me are just wrong.”

prompt.en: Which revision addresses the other side in an academic tone?
prompt.es: ¿Qué revisión trata el punto de vista contrario con un tono académico?

high.en: Frame: “Some argue that ___; however, this view overlooks ___.”
high.es: Marco: “Some argue that ___; however, this view overlooks ___.” (= “Algunos sostienen que ___; sin embargo, esta postura pasa por alto ___.”)

medium.en: State the other side fairly, then respond to it.
medium.es: Presenta el otro punto de vista con justicia y luego respóndele.

label.en: “Some argue that homework builds discipline; however, this overlooks students who work after school to help their families.”
label.es: “Some argue that homework builds discipline; however, this overlooks students who work after school to help their families.”

label.en: “Haters will say homework builds discipline or whatever, but they've obviously never had a job after school.”
label.es: “Haters will say homework builds discipline or whatever, but they've obviously never had a job after school.”
